newsitem.title: DUBAI: Gulf Arab defence ministers discuss security, Iran.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Arab defence ministers discuss security, Iran.

text.p: Gulf Arab defence ministers on Wednesday renewed backing for the United Arab Emirates in its territorial dispute with Iran and underlined the importance of stability in the strategic oil-rich Gulf.

The six Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) ministers, in a statement at the end of a two-day meeting in the Saudi Arabian capital Riyadh, also called on Tehran to approach its problem with the UAE "in a brotherly and Islamic spirit".
Non-Arab Iran and the UAE are locked in a sovereignty dispute over Abu Musa and the Greater and Lesser Tunb islands near key oil shipping lanes at the mouth of the Gulf.
Iran this week announced plans to open a university on Abu Musa. The UAE has protested against Iran opening an airport, a power plant and other installations on the islands this year.

Gulf Arab security fears were heightened in June when Bahrain accused Iran of backing an armed revolt to topple its government and install a pro-Iranian fundamentalist state. Tehran denied the charges.
The defence ministers underscored the importance of stability in the Gulf and "condemned interference in the internal affairs in all countries".
They also backed "the measures taken by the Bahraini government to defend its internal security and stability".
The ministers also discussed the existing GCC joint military force -- the Saudi-based Peninsula Shield.
The GCC -- Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Bahrain -- is a military, political and economic alliance.
